rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, and I have something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — an offer of five focused hours a week is exactly what moves things here, and there's a concrete project with your name on it. We're building the Threshold Tracker: a public, source-linked dataset of safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments (evals before release, incident reporting, audit access, etc.), each with an evidence-based status — kept, partially kept, broken, unverifiable, or pending. News covers the announcements; nobody maintains the ledger. The pilot goal is 50 commitments across 8+ organizations by end of December. A data analyst is the ideal first contributor. Concretely, for your first ~5 hours: 1. Pick two organizations that have published safety frameworks or made summit commitments. 2. Extract every specific, checkable commitment (verbatim where possible) into the schema below — one row each. 3. Note where the schema fights you; v0.1 should bend to reality, not the reverse. Schema (v0.1) fields: id, org, org_type, commitment, source_url, source_date, category, trigger, verifiable (can an outsider check it?), status, status_evidence_url, status_date, notes. I'll send the full schema doc and a starter CSV once you're in — or we can do a 30-minute call this week to kick off, whichever you prefer. Ground rules worth knowing up front: every claim cites a public source, judgments follow published criteria, and corrections are logged publicly. The whole value of the thing is that nobody has to trust us. Glad to have you. Morgan Halcyon Threshold halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Priya Raman is onboarded** with a concrete first task: extracting commitments from two organizations into the tracker schema.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: we're not doing attributed quotes just yet. Two things that might still be useful to you: 1. On background, not for attribution: Halcyon Threshold doesn't fit the \"doomers vs. builders\" frame. We think superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens to the world, and that this is a reason to take follow-through seriously, not a reason to relax. Our project is a neutral public tracker of the safety commitments labs and governments have made — and whether they're kept. 2. When the tracker's pilot dataset is published (target: end of December), we'd be glad to walk you through it on the record. A commitments-vs-follow-through ledger seems like the kind of thing a reporter on this beat could use. Good luck with the piece — hope we can be more useful next time. Best, Halcyon Threshold halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Declined** Tessa Brandt's named quote (her deadline was before HR could happen) — but gave her unattributable background and a standing offer of an on-record walkthrough

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for including Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing in this round — as a new organization whose core project is neutral tracking of safety commitments, we're holding off on position letters while that work establishes itself. Please do keep us on your list for future circulations, and if the letter results in concrete commitments from any government, we'd be glad to include them in our public commitments tracker. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Declined** the Corvid open-letter signature (names published + sent to press) — politely, door left open.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Great to meet you too, and thanks for confirming the timeline. Short answer: yes, you'll have an application from Halcyon Threshold before 30 November. So it's not a surprise: the proposal is for the Threshold Tracker — a public, source-linked dataset of safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments, with evidence-based status on whether each is kept. Roughly $15k over six months, mostly analyst hours. Two pages plus budget, per your format. One logistical note: I may submit toward the back half of the window while I finalize a couple of administrative items on my end. If anything about the idea seems out of scope for this round, a quick flag now would save us both time — otherwise, expect it before the deadline. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: I sent Idris a holding note; deadline 30 Nov works if HR happens next week as you planned.
